title: Handcuffed man dies in police custody
article: RCMP are investigating the death of a scantily clad man during an arrest early Thursday in Red Deer.
Kenneth Gordon Holt, 39, a pipefitter, was on the ground and handcuffed when it was noticed he was not breathing.
Ambulance crews failed to resuscitate him and Holt was declared dead on arrival at Red Deer Regional Hospital, said Const. Dan Doyle.
An autopsy is scheduled for today. However, toxicology tests are expected to take some time.
Holt's grief-stricken Medicine Hat family wants an inquiry into the death. They declined comment Thursday.
A provincial fatality inquiry is held in cases where people have died in custody.
At 4:30 a.m., Mounties received two calls of a man behaving strangely on 59th Street near the central Alberta city's downtown.
"They were advised that a male . . . wearing T-shirt and shorts and waving a stick around, was going around banging on doors, ringing doorbells," Doyle said.
The man was "very agitated" when officers spoke to him, then arrested him, Doyle said.
"They just used handcuffs on him, because with five (officers) there, there was no need to use any more force than that."
After they handcuffed him they tied his feet to prevent him from kicking. No pepper spray or stun guns were used to subdue him. The man was then put to the ground face down, Doyle said.
"There was nothing really out of the ordinary when it came to arrest him," he said.
"He seemed to stop struggling with police and just a short time after that (police tried) to speak to him and discovered he wasn't breathing. Of course, the handcuffs were removed."
CPR was immediately started and continued until Holt was pronounced dead at hospital.
Doyle said police are seeking answers to why Holt was agitated.
Holt had been living in Red Deer for a year-and-a-half, working at the Nova chemical plant in nearby Joffre. He was known to police but suspected of nothing serious, Doyle said.
"We know that other detachments, specifically in British Columbia, have had some dealings with him."
The southern Alberta RCMP major- crimes unit, based in Calgary, is involved in the investigation.

Cpl. Patrick Webb said the unit's involvement is standard in such cases. "They'll just investigate it as a death," he said. "They would go in, get statements and get all the evidence, because lots of times it goes to an inquiry.

"You want to get somebody in there very experienced in investigating death from outside the attachment. Not that it's suspicious or anything; (we) just want to collect up all the evidence right away."
